extracted.intended_audience: general news readers interested in fashion and culture
extracted.subtask_description: Writing a short online news article that reports a corporation's controversial product and the company's public response (apology, product withdrawal, and commitments). Focus is on timely coverage of brand backlash and contextual background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue a public apology
rubrics_metrics.description: Company 'released a statement Wednesday saying it "deeply apologizes for the offense caused."'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public-facing statement should acknowledge offense and include an explicit apology; quoting the company's wording is standard practice in reporting. Timeliness of the apology is important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdraw the offending product
rubrics_metrics.description: Luxury fashion brand Gucci 'has stopped selling a sweater that resembles blackface.' The sweater 'was being sold for $890 in Gucci stores and online before being pulled.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removing the product from stores and online is a concrete corrective action; reports should note whether and when the item was pulled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commit to internal change (diversity/learning)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gucci added: 'We are fully committed to increasing diversity throughout our organization and turning this incident into a powerful learning moment for the Gucci team and beyond.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies often accompany apologies with promises of internal reforms or training; report the specific commitments and any follow-up actions or timelines if available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge and report social media backlash
rubrics_metrics.description: The sweater 'was ridiculed on social media as insensitive and racist,' with examples such as critical tweets included in the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage should document public reaction (social media, influencers, public figures) and include representative examples to show the scale and tone of backlash.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain (or claim) intent / provide company rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Prada initially said the items were 'imaginary creatures not intended to have any reference to the real world and were "certainly not blackface."' It later apologized, saying the resemblance 'was by no means intentional.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies may claim lack of intent; reporting should record those claims and note subsequent changes in stance (e.g., later apologies or removals). This helps readers assess response credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity to timing and context
rubrics_metrics.description: The article highlights timing: 'On Black History Month....' (context suggesting increased sensitivity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports should note timing/contextual factors (holidays, anniversaries, related news) that may amplify offense or public reaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note patterns and prior similar incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: The article states: 'It's not the first time in recent months that a high-end fashion brand had been accused of carrying racist products.' It then references a recent Prada incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextualize the incident within any pattern of similar controversies to show whether this is isolated or part of a broader trend; cite prior examples and company histories where relevant.
